From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finlypay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T08:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike on hosted endpoint - production impact

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed a surge of autoscaler spin-ups in the us-west-2 hosted GPU pool starting ~07:26 UTC.
- First-token latencies on newly-provisioned GPU nodes are high: baseline first-token ~70–120ms; affected nodes showing 1.8s–4.8s (matches your traces).
- Root contributor appears to be increased cold-init time on GPU nodes after a rolling agent update pushed yesterday night. Primary symptoms: longer container image unpack + GPU driver/init step (~40–65s additional), followed by a delayed KV cache priming (adds another ~20–30s until low-latency steady state).
- We also saw intermittent throttling spikes from our image registry region, which amplified boot time for batches of nodes.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:15 UTC):
1) Reduced scale aggressiveness for new autoscaler policy to prefer existing warm capacity for 15 minutes.
2) Temporarily disabled the newest agent rollout for hosted GPU nodes to stop introducing new cold-start characteristics.
3) Enabled a short-term routing preference to keep traffic on nodes with warmed KV caches when possible.

Impact/ETA: The mitigations are live and we see p95 trending down in our internal dashboards (still stabilizing). For full recovery to pre-incident latencies we estimate 45–90 minutes as KV caches repopulate and any queued image pulls complete.

Permanent actions proposed:
- Keep a small warm pool (configurable per-customer) to reduce first-token regressions for high-QPS tenants.
- Add proactive image prefetching in our autoscaler when we detect upcoming scheduled scale events.
- Harden image registry fallback to alternate region to avoid single-region pull amplification.

I’ll continue to post updates here every ~30 minutes and will attach the detailed boot traces once sanitized.

Dev Patel
On-call Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T11:45:00Z
Subject: Customer update: mitigation applied and next steps

Carlos — quick summary for your team and for internal record:
- What happened: Rolling agent rollout + transient image-registry throttling increased GPU node cold-init time and delayed KV cache priming, which caused higher first-token latencies for newly-created nodes.
- What we did: reduced autoscaler aggressiveness, paused the rollout, enabled routing preference toward warmed nodes, and throttled new node launches while images completed pulling.
- Current status: p95/p99 are trending back toward baseline; errors have dropped to <1% for FinlyPay traffic. We’ll keep monitoring for the next 12 hours.
- Customer credit: We will apply a 10% credit for 07:30–09:00 UTC as Marissa approved. Billing will follow up with a formal memo.
- Next steps (internal): implement warm pools, image prefetch, and registry fallback as high-priority engineering work; postmortem delivers within 72 hours.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the technical details with Dev and my team, send a time and we’ll join.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep you posted.

Avery Johnson
Customer Success (Hosted) — Redwood Inference
